Voxarium Studio processes are preventing installation. End them and continue?

Running tasks will be interrupted and unsaved changes may be lost. Only processes from this installation folder will be stopped.

editor.codexHint: Runs each task as `codex exec`. Permission mode picks the sandbox (Plan reads only, Bypass permissions drops it, the rest write inside the working directory); Max turns, the tool list and the Studio's own tools do not apply, so the agent describes hand-offs in its summary. The project's MCP servers are passed on.
editor.qwenHint: Runs tasks and chats through Qwen Code with session resumption and Studio/project MCP tools. Uses Qwen authentication and the configured model by default. Plan only analyzes; Bypass permissions approves all tools; Accept edits approves file edits. Effort, Max turns, Claude plugins and named agents do not apply. Images are passed as file paths.

editor.soloModeHint: A released task waits in Pending while another of this member's tasks is in progress, and starts by itself when that one ends — lowest number first. Off, every released task runs at once.
editor.isolateHint: Each task gets its own branch so parallel members cannot collide. Ignored unless the project's version control system can provide one — git can, and tasks fall back to serialising overlapping paths where it cannot.

They live in a file that is committed with the project, and the Studio runs them for as long as it has the project open.

active.title: Active system
active.isolated: Team tasks each get their own checkout, so two agents can work at once without overwriting each other (§10.5).

choose.title: Which system to use

choose.autoHint: Checks Plastic SCM and Perforce workspaces first, then Git. You can choose a system explicitly when more than one recognises the project.
choose.builtInIsolates: built in · drives {program} · isolates agent tasks
choose.executableHint: Only needed when {program} is not on PATH — give the full path to the executable. Empty means run it by name.

fields.clientHint: The existing Perforce workspace that contains this project. Leave empty to use your Perforce configuration.

fields.perforceAuth: Authentication uses the local Perforce login ticket. Run p4 login for this server and user before connecting.

commit.title: Commit

pending.one: {count} changed file in the working copy — the Explorer's tree marks which, with a letter and a colour per file.
pending.other: {count} changed files in the working copy — the Explorer's tree marks which, with a letter and a colour per file.

commit.wholeCopy: The whole working copy — this page does not stage files one at a time.
commit.nothing: Nothing to commit — the working copy has no changes to record.

diff.title: Diff

memory.title: Memory
memory.intro: Lasting facts about this project that every agent on the team is shown, whichever runtime it uses — decisions, conventions, pitfalls, where things live. Agents add to it as they work, and you can correct it here. Each entry is a file in {folder}, committed with the project.

sharing.title: Shared with agents
sharing.enabledHint: Every task run, chat and Producer conversation opens with the index below, and agents get the recall, remember and forget tools. Switched off, agents neither see nor change it; the files stay.
sharing.capHint: From {min} to {max}. Entries past the limit are counted rather than listed, and agents read them with recall.
sharing.capInvalid: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}.

truncated.one: {count} entry does not fit — agents are told it exists and read it with recall.
truncated.other: {count} entries do not fit — agents are told how many and read them with recall.

sharing.previewEmpty: Nothing yet — agents are told memory is empty and asked to record what they learn.
sharing.off: Off — agents are told nothing about project memory.

list.title: Entries
list.emptyHint: Agents add entries with remember as they learn about the project. You can add one here too.

create.title: New entry
create.name: Name
create.nameHint: The entry’s id and file name: lower-case Latin letters, digits and hyphens. Saved as {path}.
create.nameInvalid: Use lower-case Latin letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit — at most 64 characters.
create.descriptionPlaceholder: The game targets Unreal 5.4 — plugins are pinned to it, so never upgrade one alone.
create.descriptionHint: One line, at most {max} characters: the fact and when it matters. Every agent is sent it.

import.shared: Imported entries are written to {folder} and committed with the project — leave out anything personal.
import.nothing: Nothing remembered for this project. Looked in:

import.listCut: The list is longer than can be shown; import these and open it again.

summary.other: {count} entries were not imported — the reason is on each row.

skipped.gone: No longer in the agent’s memory.
skipped.exists: An entry of that name appeared meanwhile; tick it again to replace it.

usage.title: How agents use it
usage.body: Agents read an entry with {recall}, add or correct one with {remember}, and delete one with {forget}. Changes are written straight to the project, so colleagues working in their own checkouts see them at once.
usage.note: The instruction sent with the index is the {fragment} line in {settings} → {section}.

skills.title: Skills
skills.intro: Skills from the Studio, the project and installed agents are listed here. Each skill contains a {file} and supporting files. Assign project and installed skills in the member settings on Teams. Built-in skills are available automatically. Installed and built-in files are read-only here.

list.emptyHint: Create one here, or copy a folder with a SKILL.md into {folder}.

create.descriptionHint: What it does and when to use it — the one line an agent reads before deciding to open the skill.

usage.body: A member given skills is sent, with every task run and every chat message, one line per skill: its name, its description and the path of its {file}. The agent reads that file when its work matches the description, and the other files in the folder when the instructions point to them — each skill's folder is readable by that member, even from an isolated checkout.
usage.note: Studio project skills are separate from native {dir} installations. The catalog also discovers shared and backend-specific installations. Assigned skills are described by {fragment} under {settings} → {section}.

mcp.title: MCP Servers
mcp.intro: Servers listed here are handed to every Claude agent session the Studio starts (§10.7). The file is Claude Code's own, at the project root, so the same servers are available in a terminal — and it is usually committed, which is a reason to keep tokens out of it.

agents.title: AI agents
agents.parallelHint: How many agent sessions — task runs and chats together — may talk to the model at once. A task started past this waits In progress and says so in its transcript; raising the number starts the waiting ones right away.

tasks.projectCodeHint: Goes in front of every task's number, so a task can be named out loud and in a commit message. 1–6 letters and digits, at least one letter. Leave it empty and it is derived from the project's name.

project.title: Project
project.openAnotherHint: Everything the current project has running — pipeline runs, agent sessions — stops when another one is opened.

updates.title: Studio updates
updates.noRelease: This checkout is on no release yet.

startup.label: Launch Voxarium Studio when I sign in

agentPrompts.title: Agent prompts
agentPrompts.intro: Everything the Studio itself tells an agent, beyond the roster and the brief. Reword any line, or clear it to drop it from the prompt entirely. Changes save automatically. Reset returns a line to the built-in text and keeps it following future updates.
agentPrompts.loadError: Could not load the built-in prompts: {error}
agentPrompts.cannotRemove: Cannot be removed — an empty line falls back to the default.
agentPrompts.saveBlankToRemove: Clear this line to drop it from the prompt.

identity.title: Who the member is
identity.note: Written into .claude/agents/<member>.md — the file a terminal’s claude --agent reads too — or sent with the run when no definition can be written.

system.title: Every run’s system prompt
system.note: Appended to the stock Claude Code prompt with what only that run knows.

openers.title: Messages that open a run
openers.note: What the Studio sends when it resumes or continues a session on your behalf.

chat.title: Chats with a member
chat.note: The floating chat: the same session, tools, MCP servers and Studio skill as a task run, with where you are in the Studio in place of a brief.

producer.title: Producer Mode
producer.note: Instructions for planning, decision modes, task review, budget checks and context summaries.

identity.label: Introduction
identity.hint: The line that introduces every member: their name, role and team.

identity_responsibility.label: Responsibility
identity_responsibility.hint: Sent when the member has an area of responsibility in the roster.

identity_manager.label: Manager
identity_manager.hint: Sent when the member reports to someone — names who reviews their work.

identity_reports.label: Direct reports
identity_reports.hint: Sent when anyone reports to this member.

identity_peers.label: Sideways routes
identity_peers.hint: Sent when the member may hand work to peers (their can_assign_to list).

task_context.label: Task id
task_context.hint: Tells the session which card it is working on.

task_temp.label: Temporary task files
task_temp.hint: Directs working and temporary files to {temp_dir}, the task's absolute scratch directory. Its contents are deleted when the task moves to Done.

studio_skill.label: Studio skill
studio_skill.hint: Points the session at the skill that teaches the Studio’s tools — the board, delegation, the shared documents, the code graph. Sent when the Studio’s own MCP server reaches the session; {skill} is the skill’s name. The skill itself ships with the Studio beside the tools it describes, so it is not a setting.

no_studio_tools.label: No Studio tools
no_studio_tools.hint: Sent instead of the Studio skill line when the member has routes but the Studio’s tools are disabled or unavailable.

member_skills.label: Skills
member_skills.hint: Sent when the member has been given skills on the Teams page — task runs and chats alike. {skills} is one line per skill: its name, its description and the path of its SKILL.md.

docs_location.label: Documents folder
docs_location.hint: Where the team’s shared documents live on disk.

project_memory.label: Project memory
project_memory.hint: Sent to task runs and chats while project memory is on and the Studio’s tools reach the session, also when it is empty — it asks agents to record what they learn. {entries} is the index: one line per entry, its name and description, cut at the limit set on the Memory page.

subagents.label: Subagents
subagents.hint: Sent to task runs the Studio’s tools reach; chats have no task to split and do not get it. Requires splitting the task into parallel parts and delegating them through the Studio’s subagent tools, and no subagents when the task does not split.

code_graph.label: Code graph
code_graph.hint: Sent when a graphify knowledge graph exists at the agent launch root — the Graphify plugin keeps one there. Names the graph and sends the session to the Studio skill for how to query it; {graph} is the file, {skill} the skill.

isolated_checkout.label: Isolated checkout
isolated_checkout.hint: Sent when the task runs in its own worktree, branched off the project (§10.5).

outside_project.label: Outside the project
outside_project.hint: Sent when the launch root places the session outside the project root.

finish.label: Finishing up
finish.hint: Closes the system prompt: asks for a summary for the reviewer.

finish_tool.label: Finishing up, with the tools
finish_tool.hint: Closes the system prompt when the Studio's tools reach the session: asks for finish_task with a result type — done, question or error — and the summary.

resume.label: Resume
resume.hint: Opens a resumed session when nothing new was written for it — the brief is already in its context.

resume_notes.label: Notes preamble
resume_notes.hint: Introduces the notes written since the last run stopped, right after the Resume message.

review_changes.label: Changes requested
review_changes.hint: Opens the session a reviewer sent back; {comment} is their feedback.

stall_continue.label: Continue after a stall
stall_continue.hint: Opens each automatic continuation of a session that stopped mid-work with its turn budget spent.

mid_run_message.label: Message to a working session
mid_run_message.hint: Wraps what you send to a task or a chat while its agent is working: handed over between two tool calls, or as the next turn. {message} is your text.

result_required.label: Result missing
result_required.hint: Sent once to a session that ended without calling finish_task; a session that still says nothing reaches review unlabelled.

chat_mode.label: Chat mode
chat_mode.hint: Stands where the task id would in a chat’s system prompt: this is a conversation with the user, not a card on the board.

chat_context.label: Where the user is
chat_context.hint: Opens every chat message; {context} is the page, the open document and the selected text at the moment of sending.

producer_mode.label: Producer System Prompt
producer_mode.hint: Defines the built-in Producer's responsibility and the rules for planning, approvals, scope review and waiting in Producer Mode. {language} is the initial conversation language.

producer_start.label: Start Producer Mode
producer_start.hint: Asks what the user wants to accomplish now.

producer_wake.label: Resume Producer Mode
producer_wake.hint: Resumes coordination after approval, task changes or a restart.

task_compact.label: Compress task context
task_compact.hint: Preserves decisions, completed work and pending requests in one summary for a fresh session.

producer_compact.label: Compact Producer context
producer_compact.hint: Summarizes goals, decisions and task progress for a fresh context.

producer_careful.label: Producer: Careful
producer_careful.hint: Forwards new execution questions and waits for your plan approval.

producer_independent.label: Producer: Independent
producer_independent.hint: Makes decisions and approves plans independently; escalates only critical blockers.

producer_task_cost.label: Task cost checks
producer_task_cost.hint: Tells the Producer how to compare accumulated API Cost with Estimate Task Cost before continuing a task and when to split remaining work into new tasks.

producer_review.label: Task review rules
producer_review.hint: Guides review decisions and explains how to close completed work and create follow-up tasks for corrections.

producer_state.label: Current state and task history
producer_state.hint: Adds the current Producer state and guidance for reading task history. {state} is the saved state and task board; {prompt} is the current request.

producer_summary.label: Saved conversation summary
producer_summary.hint: Restores the saved summary before a new request. {summary} is the compacted conversation; {prompt} is the current request.

producerPage.title: Producer Mode
producerPage.deleteChat: Stop Producer Mode and delete chat
producerPage.newChatHint: Create a Producer chat. Parallel chats share the team’s task board and project files.
producerPage.emptyTasksHint: Active task conversations appear here as work starts.
producerPage.noProducer: Producer is not available for this team.

tokenUsage.costHint: Total cost in USD. ≈ indicates an estimate; ≥ indicates a partially priced total.
tokenUsage.costUnavailable: The runtime did not report a cost.
tokenUsage.sentHint: Input tokens sent to the model, including cache creation. Cache reads are counted separately.
tokenUsage.receivedHint: Output tokens received from the model.
tokenUsage.unavailable: The recorded usage does not provide this token count.
tokenUsage.uncachedHint: Input, cache creation and output tokens. Cache reads are counted separately.
tokenUsage.cachedHint: Input tokens read from the cache. These are not included in tokens excluding cache reads.
tokenUsage.unclassifiedHint: Historical tokens without enough evidence to separate cache reads. They are not counted as uncached tokens.
tokenUsage.chartMetric: Token type shown in all charts

contextViewer.title: Context Viewer
contextViewer.subtitle: Explore what makes up the agent’s context
contextViewer.inspectHint: Requests the runtime’s own breakdown. Claude may contact the provider to count tokens. Qwen Code is started briefly on the saved session to run /context detail, without a model turn, and is available between turns. This action is never run automatically.
contextViewer.noText: The runtime supplied counts or metadata without the source text.
contextViewer.truncated: Preview shortened. The block size includes the complete available text.
contextViewer.nativeMethod: Block sizes use the runtime’s /context breakdown. Metadata appears where available; source text is not supplied by this command. Free capacity and deferred tools are excluded. This snapshot is replaced by local estimates when the conversation updates or you refresh.
contextViewer.partial: Some startup or runtime sources are unavailable for this session. Only retained context is shown.
contextViewer.empty: No context has been captured for this session yet.
contextViewer.zeroArea: These fragments contain zero tokens. Select a row to inspect its source.
contextViewer.expandHint: Double-click a block or scroll up over it to view its fragments.
contextViewer.backHint: Scroll down to return to the source types.
contextViewer.fragmentUnavailable: The full text is unavailable. Refresh the context to update the map.
contextViewer.otherHint: The runtime reports more input tokens than the available text explains. This part may include provider instructions, tool definitions, project files, images or history that Studio cannot inspect. Its contents and exact source breakdown are unavailable.
contextViewer.method: Block sizes estimate 1 token per 4 characters. When available, the selected backend’s journal supplies full tool results, instructions and tool definitions; its recorded compaction replaces old history. Hidden instructions, encrypted reasoning, images and tokenizer differences can still leave a gap. Retained text may differ from the latest provider request.
